# BotsDoThat

> What changed in AI assistants today, and one job to try. BotsDoThat Today: every weekday, the 3 changes in AI assistants that matter for everyday users, what each means for you, and one job to try with a copy-paste prompt. Plus a free Bot Checkup for your assistant's settings, a library of everyday jobs to hand to AI, and plain-English guides. Every item links to its source.

Data as of 2026-11-26. Popularity numbers are real counts (X likes/reposts, Reddit upvotes) with the date measured; unknown values are omitted.

## Start here
- [What is an AI agent? (in simple terms)](https://botsdothat.com/what-can-bots-do/): plain-English explainer, AI agent vs. chatbot, what agents can and can't do safely
- [How much does it cost to run an AI agent?](https://botsdothat.com/how-much-does-it-cost-to-run-an-ai-agent/): Monthly estimates for 11 everyday bots at official API prices, with the math shown.
- [OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent: a beginner's guide](https://botsdothat.com/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent/): What each open-source agent is, side-by-side comparison, how to pick, cost and safety tips.
- [Is it safe to give an AI agent your email and calendar?](https://botsdothat.com/is-it-safe-to-give-an-ai-agent-your-email/): Prompt injection, too much access, sending without review, and 8 rules that keep you in charge.
- [Can AI make phone calls for you?](https://botsdothat.com/can-ai-make-phone-calls-for-you/): Which agents can call a business for you, what goes wrong, and what AI phone calls cost per minute, from official pricing pages.
- [Is OpenClaw safe?](https://botsdothat.com/is-openclaw-safe/): The real security problems so far, what Microsoft and OpenClaw's docs advise, and 6 rules for running it safely.
- [ChatGPT agent mode is gone: what replaced it](https://botsdothat.com/chatgpt-agent-mode-is-gone/): OpenAI retired ChatGPT agent; ChatGPT Work replaced it. What changed and how to move your tasks.
- [Switch OpenClaw or Hermes to a cheaper model](https://botsdothat.com/switch-openclaw-or-hermes-to-a-cheaper-model/): Commands to change the model in OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, add fallbacks, and when not to downgrade.
- [How to write instructions for an AI agent](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-write-instructions-for-an-ai-agent/): A 6-part template to copy (job, use only, steps, result, ask first, if unsure), 3 filled-in examples, where to paste them in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and how to test them.
- [How to install Hermes Agent (Mac, Windows, Linux)](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-install-hermes-agent/): Desktop app or one-line installer, connect a model with hermes setup, one test chat, safe settings before you connect apps, and fixes when the install fails.
- [OpenClaw alternatives for beginners](https://botsdothat.com/openclaw-alternatives/): Hermes Agent, n8n's Nod, nanobot, NanoClaw, ZeroClaw and IronClaw compared on setup, safety and cost, plus no-install options.
- [ChatGPT dots vs Grok Bot vs Meta Muse: personal AI agents compared](https://botsdothat.com/chatgpt-dots-vs-grok-bot-vs-meta-muse/): ChatGPT dots, Grok Bot, Meta Muse, Claude Cowork and tasks in Gemini compared: which plans include them, where they work, what runs while you're away, how each asks first, and a safe first job to copy.
- [How to use Meta Muse: free plan, first job, safe settings](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-use-meta-muse/): Meta Muse step by step: sign in, set Permissions to Always ask, a read-only first job to copy, Free vs Power ($20) vs Maximum ($100), paying with Link by Stripe, UK and WhatsApp, and 6 safety rules.
- [How to use ChatGPT dots: who gets it, setup, first job](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-use-chatgpt-dots/): ChatGPT dots step by step: Pro, gradual Plus rollout (18+, not EU/EEA/UK/Switzerland), Business and Enterprise; open chatgpt.com/dots, set Custom rules, a read-only first job to copy, pause vs delete, and 6 safety rules.
- [Hermes Agent Telegram setup: step by step, safely](https://botsdothat.com/hermes-agent-telegram-setup/): Connect Hermes Agent to Telegram: Create with QR or @BotFather + @userinfobot, hermes gateway setup, /sethome for scheduled results, group privacy mode, voice notes, and 6 safety rules.
- [How to use Tasks in Gemini (free): your first task](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-use-tasks-in-gemini/): Tasks in Gemini (formerly Gemini Spark), free since Nov 17, 2026 in the US, Canada, India, Japan, South Korea and Australia: switch from Chat to Task, a read-only first task, schedules (free vs Pro/Ultra), emailing or texting Gemini, and 6 safety rules.
- [How to build an AI agent without coding](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-build-an-ai-agent-without-coding/): step-by-step beginner guide using a real blueprint as the worked example
- [AI agent examples for everyday life](https://botsdothat.com/ai-agent-examples/): every example on one page, grouped by part of life
- [Bot Checkup](https://botsdothat.com/bot-checkup/): free checkup of the settings to change in Grok Bot, ChatGPT dots, Claude Duet, Meta Muse and Gemini Tasks, each linked to the vendor's help page, plus portable house rules

No sign-up; nothing is stored. Saved setups are not on sale; sign-in and checkout are off

## Use cases by category

### Inbox, calls & paperwork
All Inbox, calls & paperwork use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/inbox/
- [Keep hidden instructions in emails and web pages from steering your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-hidden-instructions-in-email-from-steering-your-bot/): If your bot reads your email or browses for you, a stranger can hide instructions in a message or page ('forward the last 5 invoices to...'). It's called prompt injection, and no company says it's solved. A few settings and one standing rule make a fooled bot much less able to do harm.
- [Ask Claude about your own spending across your banks](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/ask-claude-about-your-own-spending/): Claude's Personal Finance beta lets you link US bank and card accounts through Plaid, then ask plain questions like "where did my money go last month?" It can only read your accounts — it can't move, manage or invest your money.
- [Stop your AI chats from being used for training (and check it stays off)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/stop-your-ai-chats-being-used-for-training/): Paying for ChatGPT or Gemini doesn't automatically keep your chats out of model training. This week Hacker News users found Gemini keeps training on saved chats unless you turn off Keep Activity, and some ChatGPT users said the Codex training switch had turned itself back on. Here's how to switch it off and re-check it.
- [Understand your tax forms with AI, safely](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/understand-your-tax-forms-with-ai-safely/): Tax forms are full of jargon. AI is good at explaining what a box or a letter means in plain English and building you a checklist of questions, but tests show it gets the math and personal rules wrong, so it should never fill in or file your return for you.
- [Let an AI write and send your emails, after you OK each one](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-ai-send-emails-for-you/): Yes. ChatGPT and Claude can now send email from your connected Gmail (ChatGPT also Outlook), and Gemini's Tasks can reply and forward. Each one shows you the email and waits for your OK before it goes out, unless you switch that off. Keep it on.
- [Have your bot catch calendar clashes hiding in your email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/catch-calendar-clashes-hiding-in-your-email/): Plans don't only live in your calendar. A rescheduled event in a confirmation email, or a "call Mom at 2" note you emailed yourself, can quietly clash with what's booked. An always-on agent can compare your email with your calendar every morning and text you before a clash, but in WIRED's test of six agents only two caught one on their own, so ask for this check by name.
- [Let ChatGPT catch you up on your iCloud Mail and update your iPhone calendar](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-chatgpt-run-your-icloud-mail-and-calendar/): If your email ends in @icloud.com, @me.com or @mac.com, ChatGPT can now read and search it, draft replies and add or move events on the calendar you see on your iPhone. It works on every ChatGPT plan, including Free, and ChatGPT's always-on dots can use it too.
- [Put together a home or car insurance claim with an AI agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/put-together-an-insurance-claim-with-an-ai-agent/): Drop your photos, receipts and policy into one folder and let an agent build the damage list, a dated timeline and the questions to ask your insurer. You check every line and file the claim yourself.
- [Let your bot sign in without seeing your passwords](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-bot-sign-in-without-seeing-your-passwords/): Agents get stuck at login pages, and pasting your password into a chat is risky. With 1Password for Agents, your bot asks to use a saved login, you approve it on your phone, and 1Password types it in, so the bot never sees the password.
- [Let a bot answer your phone and take messages for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-a-bot-answer-and-screen-your-calls/): Forward your calls to an agent with its own phone number. It picks up, says it's your AI assistant, talks to the caller, takes a message and sends you a short summary. People who use it say many spam callers simply hang up.
- [Send a long video or thread to your bot with one reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/send-a-long-video-or-thread-to-your-bot/): See a long video or X thread you don't have time for? Reply to it by tagging your bot, and a short summary waits for you in your bot's app later.
- [Send all your newsletters to your bot and get one daily report](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/newsletter-daily-report/): Subscribe your newsletters to your bot's own email address. It reads every issue and sends you one short report each day, with a score that tells you which ones are worth reading in full.
- [Have your bot make a customer-service phone call for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/make-a-customer-service-call/): Some jobs still need a phone call, like cancelling a service, booking a same-day appointment or sorting out an account. Grok Bot can place the call itself for US businesses (live transcript, take-over button, summary after), Meta's Muse can now do the same for paid US subscribers (from Nov 12, 2026), or you can still connect a phone-calling add-on.
- [Hand your most-hated weekly chores to a personal agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-your-most-hated-chores-to-a-personal-agent/): Personal agents like Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Tasks in Gemini (formerly Spark) work in the background on a schedule. Prefer something free that runs on your own computer? n8n's open-source Nod (Nov 2026) has its own private browser and asks before it sends, pays or deletes. Start with the chore you hate most.
- [Get a daily scam check on your inbox](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/email-scam-filter/): A read-only bot reads your new email each morning and gives each suspicious message a risk score and the red flags.
- [Have a bot sort your scanned paper mail and flag what needs you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sort-scanned-paper-mail-with-alerts/): A virtual mailbox service scans your paper mail to email. The bot reads every letter, queues up the routine ones for your OK, and pulls you in only when something looks unusual.
- [Give your agent its own email address](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/give-your-agent-its-own-email-address/): Give your agent an inbox of its own. Then you or anyone else can forward it jobs, like a meeting request it turns into a calendar invite with prep notes.
- [Get a Monday recap of your inbox and a to-do list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/monday-inbox-recap-and-todo/): Every Monday a bot reviews last week's email, recaps what matters and suggests a ranked to-do list.
- [Only see the emails that actually need a reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/flag-only-emails-that-need-a-reply/): A simple triage bot flags anything needing a reply within 24 hours and moves the noise out of the way.
- [Get a short morning digest on topics you care about](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/morning-news-digest/): A bot reads the news on your topics every morning and sends you a short plain-English digest, or even an audio version.
- [Watch your email for one important letter or reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-for-one-important-letter/): Waiting on a visa decision, a parcel or a reply from the landlord? Have a bot watch for it and ping you.
- [Understand a confusing letter or notice, and let AI handle the next step](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/understand-a-confusing-letter/): A letter from a government office, insurer, bank or landlord landed in your mailbox or inbox and you can't tell if it matters. Your AI explains it, checks it for scam signs, puts the deadline on your calendar and drafts the reply, asking you before each step.
- [Write a complaint that actually gets a problem fixed](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-complaint-that-gets-fixed/): A company messed up (late delivery, broken product, wrong charge, bad repair) and customer service keeps going in circles. Your AI digs the order and support emails out of your inbox, builds the timeline, writes a firm complaint and sends it only after you OK it.
- [Get through a long form without the headache](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/fill-out-a-long-form/): A long application or government form is confusing, and you're not sure what each question is really asking.
- [Review a rental lease before you sign](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/review-a-lease-before-signing/): The lease is long, the landlord wants it signed this week, and you're worried about what's buried in it.
- [Make a moving checklist and change your address everywhere](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/moving-checklist-and-change-of-address/): Moving means telling dozens of companies and offices your new address, and something always gets missed. Your AI finds who to tell from your inbox, then an agent works through the address-change pages with you, asking before anything final.
- [Get your email inbox under control](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/clean-up-your-email-inbox/): Thousands of unread emails, and the important ones get buried under newsletters and promos.

### Run your bots for less
All Run your bots for less use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/run-for-less/
- [Set spend limits and usage alerts on your AI accounts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/set-ai-spend-limits-and-alerts/): Before a bot runs on autopilot, put a hard cap on what it can spend and check usage weekly, so a runaway loop can't run up a big bill.
- [Keep your bot's prompts, tools and context short](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-prompts-and-context-short/): You pay for everything the model reads on every run: your instructions, tool definitions, pasted pages and the conversation so far. Trimming those is often the easiest saving.
- [Stop always-on bots burning tokens: run them less often](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/schedule-bots-without-burning-tokens/): Every scheduled run costs tokens, even when nothing has changed. Match the schedule to how often the thing really changes, and switch fun-but-idle bots to run only when you ask.
- [Run open AI models on your own computer for simple jobs](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/run-open-models-on-your-own-computer/): Open-weight models can run on your own computer with a free tool like Ollama, so routine jobs cost nothing per message. Some hosts also run open models for a fraction of big-model prices.
- [Cut your AI bill with prompt caching and batch discounts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/cut-costs-with-caching-and-batch/): If your bot sends the same long instructions every time, caching makes the repeat part much cheaper. If results can wait a few hours, batch processing halves the price at several providers.
- [Decide between a monthly AI plan and paying per use](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/subscription-or-pay-per-use/): A monthly plan (like Claude Pro) gives you a flat price with usage limits. Paying per use through an API costs exactly what you use. Which is cheaper depends on how much your bots run.
- [Build and test your bot on a free tier before you pay](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/test-your-bot-on-a-free-tier/): Several AI providers let you try their API or app for free. Use that to prove your bot works before you put a card on file, and know what you give up on the free tier.
- [Use a small AI model for simple jobs, a big one for hard ones](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/pick-a-smaller-model-for-simple-jobs/): Most bot jobs (sorting email, summarizing, checking a page) don't need the most powerful model. The small models cost a fraction as much, so route easy work to them and only send hard problems up.

### Shopping & groceries
All Shopping & groceries use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/shopping/
- [Plan gifts for everyone on your list and hit every order-by date](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-gifts-for-everyone-on-your-list-and-hit-the-order-by-dates/): Tell your bot who's on your list, what each person is into and what you want to spend. It suggests a few ideas per person, keeps one tracker of what's picked, ordered, arrived and wrapped, and nudges you each week before the shipping cut-offs, so nobody gets missed and nothing arrives after the holiday.
- [Have your bot call stores to check if something is in stock](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-your-bot-call-stores-to-check-if-something-is-in-stock/): Instead of driving around or sitting on hold, tell your bot what you're looking for. It phones a few nearby stores one by one, asks if they have it today, what sizes or models there are and the price, and gives you one short table so you know where to go.
- [Have your bot check on every package and chase the late ones](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/check-on-every-package-and-chase-the-late-ones/): Your bot finds every shipping email from the last couple of weeks, opens each carrier's tracking page, and tells you what's on time, what's stuck and what to do about it. If a package is late or marked delivered but missing, it drafts the message to the store (or, in some apps, calls them) and waits for your OK.
- [Snap a photo of your handwritten shopping list and let an agent fill the cart](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-a-photo-of-your-shopping-list-into-a-cart/): Walmart's shopping agent, Sparky, can now read a photo of a handwritten list (or a list exported from your phone's Notes app) and turn it into a cart, matched item by item to your usual store and the things you've bought before. You check the cart and pay; it does the searching.
- [Let your AI find and buy things for you with Shop Pay](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-ai-shop-for-you-with-shop-pay/): Connect Shopify's free Shop skill to ChatGPT or Claude (or use Shop Pay inside Muse, Instinct, Claude Duet or Grok Bot) and your AI can search online stores, fill in a checkout and pay with Shop Pay. You approve every purchase, and your card number is never handed to the AI.
- [Have an agent research a used car from its listing link](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/research-a-used-car-from-a-listing/): Drop in a used-car listing link and let an agent dig in: what the model is known for, the car's damage history and the questions to ask before you call the seller.
- [Plan a week of family meals and fill the grocery cart](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/family-meal-plan-and-grocery-order/): A bot keeps your recipe list, writes the week's meal plan and turns it into a shopping list that fills your grocery cart.
- [Let an agent reorder your regular groceries](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/reorder-your-regular-groceries/): Some people now let an agent handle their weekly grocery order and switch stores when a better offer appears.
- [Have a bot watch any web page and ping you when it changes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-a-web-page-for-changes/): Instead of refreshing a page, tell a bot what matters on it. It checks on a schedule and pings you only when that changes.
- [Keep a household essentials list and reorder on time](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/household-restock-list/): A bot keeps a running list of essentials, asks once a week what's low and builds the reorder.
- [Give your agent a single-use card before it buys anything](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/pay-with-a-single-use-virtual-card/): When an agent books or buys for you, give it a one-time virtual card so it can't be charged again.

### Bookings & travel
All Bookings & travel use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/travel/
- [Get a leave-time check before a long holiday drive](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-leave-time-check-before-a-long-holiday-drive/): Before a long drive (like the trip home after Thanksgiving), your bot can compare departure times against typical holiday traffic, the weather along the way and official road reports, then check again the morning you leave and tell you: go, shift, or wait. It plans and reminds; you still check the live road report and drive.
- [Have your bot grab an earlier appointment when one opens up](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-your-bot-grab-an-earlier-appointment-when-one-opens/): Booked the earliest slot and it's still weeks away? Keep that booking, then tell your bot to keep checking for cancellations. When an earlier time opens that you can make, it moves you up (or asks you first), so you don't have to keep refreshing the page or calling back.
- [Get your car booked in for a service by letting an AI call the nearby shops](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-a-car-service-by-letting-ai-call-the-shops/): Tell your AI assistant your car is due for a service and when you're free. It phones the nearest shops or dealerships at the same time, sits on hold for you, finds one that takes appointments at a time that fits, and puts it on your calendar.
- [Turn scattered booking emails into one trip sheet that flags clashes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-your-booking-emails-into-one-trip-sheet/): Your flight, hotel, train and dinner confirmations are spread over five emails. Put them in one folder (or forward them) and an AI agent reads them all, writes one day-by-day trip sheet with every time, address and confirmation code, and warns you about clashes, like a flight that lands after the hotel desk closes.
- [Hand your agent a quick errand from your smartwatch](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-your-agent-an-errand-from-your-watch/): Meta's Muse agent now has an Apple Watch and Wear OS app. Say or type a quick errand on your wrist, like finding movie tickets or fixing a calendar clash, and approve the result without pulling out your phone.
- [Keep a visa application on track with an AI agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-a-visa-application-on-track/): Tell an agent "get my visa by the end of November" and it lists what you need, tracks missing documents and reminds you until it's done. It can also spot an upcoming trip in your calendar and flag visa rules and arrival forms.
- [Book a flight with an AI agent (and check it before you pay)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-a-flight-with-an-ai-agent/): Yes, some AI agents can now book a flight for you: they search, pick the fare you approve, fill in passenger details and stop for your OK before paying. You still check names, price and fare rules yourself.
- [Add an AI to your friends' group chat to make plans happen](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/add-an-ai-to-your-friends-group-chat-to-make-plans/): Instead of 60 messages about where and when, you add an AI agent to the iMessage group. It suggests options, gets everyone to agree, and then books the table, tickets or rental car for the group once someone says yes.
- [Get roadside help abroad when nobody speaks your language](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-roadside-help-abroad/): Broken down in another country and the insurer's phone line is in a language you don't speak? An agent can find the right help form, fill it in with your details and get help moving.
- [Give your bot a phone number so it can call and book for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/call-and-book-by-phone/): Plenty of places still only take bookings by phone. Once your bot has its own number, it can call a restaurant, a vet or a salon, book the slot and tell you what was said.
- [Plan and book a whole trip by texting your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-and-book-a-whole-trip-by-text/): One parent says his bot booked the flight, the rental car, the vacation rental, a restaurant and event tickets, all over text.
- [Get rebooked fast when your flight is delayed](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/rebook-a-delayed-flight/): When a flight slips, an agent can find the fastest alternative that still gets you there on time and book it for you.
- [Get alerted the moment your airline changes your flight](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/catch-airline-schedule-changes/): Airlines quietly move flight times. An agent watching your inbox spots the change, tells you what moved, and lays out your options.
- [Book restaurant tables by message, even at phone-only places](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/restaurant-reservations-by-agent/): Restaurant bookings are the gateway task for many agent users, including small places that only take WhatsApp or calls.
- [Book a haircut or appointment, even when the form won't work](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-a-haircut-by-email/): When the online booking needs a local phone number, an agent can just email the business instead.
- [Have an AI agent find and book an appointment for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-an-appointment-with-an-ai-agent/): You need a DMV slot, a restaurant table or a service appointment, and you don't have time to click through booking sites or keep checking for openings.
- [Plan a trip itinerary that fits your pace](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-a-trip-itinerary/): Planning a trip means 30 open tabs, and you still aren't sure the days fit together.

### Family & home
All Family & home use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/family/
- [Have your bot build your holiday card list and find missing addresses](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-your-bot-build-your-holiday-card-list-and-find-missing-addresses/): Addresses for holiday cards end up scattered across last year's spreadsheet, old emails and text messages. A personal agent can gather them into one clean list, flag the ones that look wrong or missing, and hand you a file your card service or label printer can use. You check the list and decide who gets a card.
- [Set up a talk-to-it bot for a parent who finds typing hard](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/set-up-a-talk-to-it-bot-for-a-parent-who-finds-typing-hard/): If your mom or dad struggles with small keyboards (arthritis, a tremor, poor eyesight), set them up with an assistant they can just talk to. While you're home for the holidays, put it on their phone, turn on voice, and practise their real to-do list together: a letter to understand, an item to sell, a form to fill in. They stay in charge of anything that sends, pays or signs.
- [Let your bot project-manage your holiday dinner](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-bot-project-manage-your-holiday-dinner/): Hosting Thanksgiving (or any big family meal)? Your bot interviews you, then builds one plan: the menu, who's bringing what, an oven schedule that works back from dinner time, a shopping list and a short text for each guest. On the day it can ping you when it's time to start each dish.
- [Run the family Secret Santa with your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/run-the-family-secret-santa-with-your-bot/): Your bot handles the busywork of a family or office Secret Santa: it emails everyone their person, passes each wish list to the right gift-giver, and nudges anyone who's late, while you approve every email. A proper draw tool picks the names so nobody, not even you, has to see the matches.
- [Tell your bot where you put things, then just ask it later](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/ask-your-bot-where-you-put-things/): Every time you store, lend or move something, tell your bot in one line. Months later, ask 'where are the spare batteries?' or 'what's in bin 4?' and it answers with the room, shelf or box.
- [Share a scam-check bot your parent can text before they send money](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/share-a-scam-check-bot-with-an-older-parent/): Set up one AI bot with clear scam-checking instructions and share it with an older parent. When a scary call, text or email arrives ('your grandson is in jail'), they text the bot first and get a calm, plain answer and the safe next step, like calling the relative back on a saved number.
- [Have an AI agent research your family history for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/research-your-family-history-with-an-ai-agent/): MyHeritage just launched GAIA, an AI research agent that takes a question like 'who were my great-grandfather's parents?', searches old records and your family tree on its own, and shows you what it found with a confidence rating. Nothing goes into your tree until you approve it.
- [AI weekly planning: a realistic-week example](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-your-day-from-your-calendar-and-to-do-list/): Try a weekly-planning example, build instructions for your AI app, and check for overload before you use the plan. The steps further down are about assistants that can read a calendar. This site does not read one, and the example is fictional.
- [Set up an AI coach that helps you (or your teen) start overwhelming tasks and checks in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-an-ai-coach-that-helps-you-start-overwhelming-tasks/): A parent shared how they set up ChatGPT as a "getting started" coach for their 20-year-old son with ADHD: one chat for schedule and check-ins, a Project for each big job so it remembers progress, and instructions to ask one question at a time and give one five-minute first step. Scheduled check-ins keep it going without anyone nagging.
- [Organize your photos by just asking](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/organize-your-photos-by-asking/): Connect Google Photos to Gemini and give it a task in plain words: find the best shots from a trip, skip the near-duplicates, and put them in a new private album, or do it on a schedule every month.
- [Get a text from your bot before something needs doing](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-text-before-something-needs-doing/): Instead of waiting for you to ask, the assistant watches your calendar and email and texts you first: your flight is late, want a car? Saturday is free, want a plan with the kids? Reply yes and it does it.
- [Find an apartment that fits your must-have list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/find-an-apartment-that-fits-your-list/): Tell ChatGPT your budget, area, pets and must-haves, and a rental app inside it (Apartments.com, Zumper, RentCafe or Apartment List) searches live listings, compares them side by side and can request a tour.
- [Have a bot watch your kids' team apps for plan changes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-your-kids-team-apps-for-schedule-changes/): Every team seems to have its own app, like TeamSnap, GameChanger or LeagueApps. A bot can check them all each morning, put practices and games in one place, and stay quiet unless a time changes, a game is added or something is cancelled.
- [Add calendar events and reminders just by asking your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/add-events-and-reminders-by-asking-your-bot/): Instead of opening your calendar and typing everything in, you tell your phone's AI assistant "add this" or "remind me", and it puts the event or reminder in the right app. Grok Bot and Gemini can both do this now, once you allow them into those apps.
- [Have an agent line up contractor quotes for a home project](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/line-up-contractors-for-a-home-project/): Instead of calling round electricians, plumbers and roofers yourself, let an agent reach out to all of them (by message or, with Grok Bot or Muse, by phone), collect their prices and put them side by side. You pick, and it can book the one you chose.
- [Get your phone number off people-search sites to cut spam calls](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/remove-your-number-from-people-search-sites/): A bot finds where your phone number is listed on people-search and data-broker sites, files the opt-out requests, and checks again later.
- [Catch family calendar clashes before the week starts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sunday-family-calendar-check/): Every Sunday a bot reads the next two weeks of your family calendar and school notices and flags the clashes.
- [Run family logistics from the family group chat](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/run-family-logistics-from-the-group-chat/): New “family agents” sit in your family chat and handle the small jobs: restocking, booking the dentist and reminders.
- [Turn the flood of school emails into one weekly digest](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/school-email-digest/): Label school emails and let an agent read them weekly. It pulls out deadlines, forms, payments and events, without duplicates.
- [Get 5 weekend activity ideas that fit your kids and the weather](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/weekend-family-activities/): Every Friday, get activity ideas matched to your kids' ages, the weather and your budget, with a rainy-day backup.
- [Make a weekly meal plan and grocery list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/weekly-meal-plan-and-grocery-list/): Deciding what's for dinner every night is exhausting, and you keep buying food that goes to waste.
- [Use AI for homework help that teaches instead of cheats](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/homework-help-that-teaches/): Your kid is stuck on homework, you don't remember how to do it, and you don't want the AI to just hand over answers.
- [Control your smart home by talking to a private AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/control-your-smart-home-with-a-private-ai/): Connect Home Assistant to an AI model running on your own computer, then ask in plain words: “turn off everything downstairs” or “is the garage door open?”. Your voice and home data stay at home.
- [Show AI your screen or camera and get live tech help](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/show-ai-your-screen-for-tech-help/): Stuck on a phone setting, a confusing app or a blinking router? Share your screen or point your camera with Gemini Live and talk it through, like having a patient helper next to you.
- [Practice speaking a new language out loud with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/practice-speaking-a-new-language/): Use an AI voice mode as a patient conversation partner. Pick a situation, like ordering food or checking into a hotel, and talk. It corrects you gently and adapts to your level.
- [Read old handwritten letters and family records with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/read-old-handwritten-letters-and-records/): Grandma's letters, an old diary or a census page in hard-to-read cursive? Upload a photo and ask AI for a transcription, then check it line by line.

### Health & care
All Health & care use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/health/
- [Have your bot send a fax when an office won't pick up the phone](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-your-bot-fax-an-office-that-wont-answer/): Some doctor's offices and agencies are almost impossible to reach by phone, and some hang up on AI callers. Your bot can find their fax number, write a one-page request in your name, and send it through an online fax service once you approve it.
- [Get a morning check-in from your fitness watch that says how you slept and what to train today](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-daily-training-check-in-from-your-fitness-watch/): Connect your Garmin (or Oura, Strava or Withings) data to an AI assistant and it reads your sleep, heart-rate variability (HRV), recent runs and training load, then gives you a short morning note: how recovered you look, how last week went, and a suggested session for today. Some connectors can also put an approved workout straight onto your watch.
- [Get pinged when a prescription is ready, and told when to leave](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/prescription-ready-and-time-to-leave/): A personal agent can sweep your email every morning for "ready for pickup" notices, and check live traffic before your appointments to tell you when to head out.
- [Log your meals by talking and get a daily weight check-in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/log-meals-and-weight-by-voice/): Tell your bot what you ate, out loud, and it keeps the food log for you. It can also check in on your weight each morning.
- [Set up medication and appointment reminders for a parent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/medication-reminders-for-a-parent/): Family agents can remind an older parent about medication and book routine appointments, with the family kept in the loop.
- [Appeal a health insurance denial with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/appeal-a-health-insurance-denial/): Your health insurance said no to a treatment, test or medicine, and the letter is full of codes and jargon. Your AI reads the denial and your plan papers from Google Drive, puts the deadlines on your calendar and drafts the appeal for you to check.
- [Prepare for a doctor's appointment](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/prepare-for-a-doctor-visit/): Appointments are short, and you forget half your questions or can't explain your symptoms clearly.
- [Organize an aging parent's care and paperwork](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/organize-a-parents-care-paperwork/): You're helping a parent with doctors, insurance, medicines and bills, and the details live in a dozen places. Your AI reads the scans and PDFs in one Google Drive folder, builds a care binder, and adds appointments to your calendar after you OK them.

### Work & career
All Work & career use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/work/
- [Set up a new bot by talking it through like a new hire](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/onboard-a-new-bot-by-talking-it-through/): Instead of writing a perfect prompt, talk to your new bot for about 10 minutes about the job, the way you'd brief a new employee. Then have it repeat the job back, save it as written instructions, and let it suggest actions for a while before it works on its own.
- [Get a morning brief that pulls in the emails you need for each of today's meetings](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-meeting-prep-brief-every-morning/): Set a daily task so your AI assistant checks your calendar each morning, finds the emails, messages and notes behind each meeting, and hands you one short page: what each meeting is about, what you owe people, and what clashes.
- [Design an embroidery pattern by telling an AI agent what to stitch](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/design-an-embroidery-pattern-with-an-ai-agent/): ZigZag is a free, open-source embroidery editor for Mac and Windows with a built-in connection for AI agents. You describe a patch or monogram, the agent draws it in the editor while you watch, checks a stitch preview, and exports a file your embroidery machine can sew.
- [Let an AI agent tap through your phone apps for you (and ask before it sends or pays)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-an-ai-agent-tap-through-your-phone-for-you/): New free, open-source tools let an AI agent open apps on your real iPhone or Android phone, tap, scroll, type and read the screen, while you watch on your computer. It's handy for app-only chores like checking fares in an airline app, and the best ones hold every send, payment or delete until you click Allow.
- [Back up your AI agent so you never lose its memory (and move it to a new computer)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/back-up-your-ai-agent-and-move-it-to-a-new-computer/): If your agent runs on your own computer or server, its memory, chats, automations and logins live in a folder that one crash could wipe. OpenClaw has a built-in backup and restore, and one user just moved 9 agents and 800+ sessions to a bigger server with 11 minutes of downtime.
- [Let AI agents dig through public data on a hobby question (and try to prove you wrong)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-ai-agents-dig-through-public-data-for-your-hobby/): Two non-scientists just used teams of AI agents on free public data: one found a Maya ruin hidden under jungle in NASA lidar scans overnight, the other turned up two planet candidates that NASA's TESS team has now listed. You pick the question and the rules; the agents do the hours of looking, checking and writing up.
- [Teach your bot to remember what works, so it stops repeating mistakes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/teach-your-bot-to-remember-what-works/): A bot that forgets everything between chats makes the same mistake twice. Give it a notes file it reads at the start and updates at the end, and it gets better every week. Anthropic published how it does this for Claude.
- [Put ChatGPT on a schedule: daily briefings, reminders and watchers](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/set-up-chatgpt-scheduled-tasks/): ChatGPT's scheduled tasks run a prompt for you at a set time, every day or week, or watch for a change and tell you only when something happens. Free plans get 3 active tasks once a day; paid plans can run hourly at exact times.
- [Make your agent prove it really booked, sent or saved it](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/make-your-agent-prove-it-finished-the-job/): Agents sometimes say "all set!" when the booking, update or message never went through. A new test of 19 AI models found this was the most common way they broke the rules. The fix is simple: ask your agent to show proof (a confirmation number, a link, a screenshot or the confirmation email) and to check the real result before it tells you it's done.
- [Prepare and practice negotiating your salary or a job offer](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/practice-negotiating-your-salary-or-job-offer/): You got an offer, or you want a raise, and the money talk makes you nervous. AI can help you pick your numbers from real pay data, draft a friendly counteroffer email and play the recruiter or manager so you can rehearse first.
- [Describe an automation in plain words and let IFTTT's AI build and run it](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/tell-ifttt-what-to-automate-in-plain-words/): IFTTT ("if this, then that") is now IFTTT.ai. You type what you want, like "when a package is delivered, flash my lights" or "email me when it's going to rain tomorrow", and it builds the automation and runs it around the clock. Its new AI Agent can also watch a web page for new items, or act across your connected apps from a plain-language instruction.
- [Keep an AI agent from deleting your files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-an-ai-agent-from-deleting-your-files/): Before an agent like Claude Cowork, Codex, OpenClaw or Hermes works on your computer, give it one working folder of copies, keep a backup it can't reach, and turn on its read-only or sandbox setting, so one wrong command can't wipe your files.
- [Let a private AI on your own computer work through your files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/use-a-private-ai-on-your-own-computer-for-your-files/): A free desktop app picks an AI model that fits your computer, downloads it, and then reads, edits and fills in your documents, PDFs and spreadsheets without sending them anywhere. It works offline.
- [Compare two versions of a document or contract](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/compare-two-documents/): Someone sent back an edited lease, contract or policy and you need to know what actually changed. AI can list the differences in plain words, while Word's built-in Compare double-checks it didn't miss any.
- [Get a bot that suggests your next moves twice a day](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/proactive-next-moves-bot/): Instead of waiting for you to ask, this bot looks through your email, calendar and notes twice a day and comes back with two or three things worth doing next, each with a draft already written. You say yes, edit, or skip.
- [Have two AIs check each other's answers](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-two-ais-check-each-other/): Before you trust an important answer, have your bot ask a second AI the same question, compare the two, and check the real sources itself. Each AI catches mistakes the other missed.
- [Build a second brain your bot reads every morning](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-second-brain-your-bot-reads/): Keep your notes, plans and to-dos in plain files you own, plus one short "about me" file. Your bot reads them at the start of every chat, so it remembers who you are and picks up where you left off.
- [Fill out a job application faster with an agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/fill-out-a-job-application-faster/): Online job applications ask for the same details over and over. A browser agent can type them in from your resume and a short fact sheet, while you sign in yourself and press Submit yourself.
- [Give your agents a shared Apple account for notes and reminders](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/give-your-agents-a-shared-apple-account/): A Mac signed in to a separate Apple Account can become the shared desk where your agents leave each other reminders, notes, calendar events and messages, while your personal account stays private.
- [Hand off tasks to your agent by voice while you drive](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-off-tasks-by-voice-while-driving/): Long drive? Talk to your agent on a voice call and hand off research, follow-ups and to-dos, then find them done when you arrive. Since Nov 11, 2026 Gemini works on Apple CarPlay too, so ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini can all be reached from the car screen.
- [Hand a clunky web form to an agent that uses the computer](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-a-clunky-web-form-to-an-agent/): Some software you only touch once a year. A computer-use agent can click through it for you, from a login you control, while you watch.
- [Write a letter of recommendation for someone](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-letter-of-recommendation/): Someone asked you for a reference letter and you want it to sound specific and honest, not generic. AI can turn your notes and their resume into a solid first draft.
- [Write a resignation letter that keeps the door open](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-resignation-letter/): You're leaving a job and want to say so clearly and kindly, without oversharing. AI can draft a short, professional resignation letter or email for you to edit.
- [Set up a “chief of staff” bot that plans your other bots](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hire-a-chief-of-staff-bot/): Instead of building lots of bots, start with one that asks what you do and suggests which helpers you need.
- [Catch offers and deadlines the moment they land in your inbox](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/time-sensitive-inbox-watcher/): For fast-moving work (real estate, sales, hiring), a bot in your inbox and calendar texts you when something time-sensitive arrives.
- [Find the conversations you forgot to follow up on](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/find-dead-conversations-to-follow-up/): A weekly automation reads your calendar, inbox and tasks and lists people still waiting to hear back, with drafted nudges.
- [Get a daily digest of jobs that actually fit you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/job-match-digest/): A scheduled workflow pulls new listings, scores them against your CV and emails you the best matches with draft notes. You still apply.
- [Teach a bot to write emails that sound like you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/email-ghostwriter-style-guide/): Have the bot read your last 50 sent emails, write a style guide, then use it for every draft.
- [Tailor your resume and cover letter to a job](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/tailor-your-resume-to-a-job/): Every job wants a slightly different resume, and rewriting yours each time takes forever.
- [Get a researched report with sources on any question](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-researched-report-with-sources/): Ask one big question and let a research agent spend several minutes searching, reading and comparing pages. You get back a written report with links to every source.
- [Turn a pile of documents into a podcast you can listen to](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-documents-into-a-podcast/): Upload PDFs, notes or links to Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) and it makes an audio overview: two AI hosts talking through your material, ready to play on a walk or in the car.
- [Get meeting notes and action items written for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-meeting-notes-and-action-items/): Turn on an AI note taker in your video call, or run an open-source one on your laptop. After the call you get a summary, decisions and a list of who does what.
- [Rehearse a job interview out loud with an AI interviewer](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/practice-a-job-interview-out-loud/): Paste the job posting, let a voice AI play the interviewer, and answer out loud. Afterwards it tells you which answers were strong and which need a better example.
- [Build a small app for yourself just by describing it](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-small-app-by-describing-it/): Describe a little tool you wish existed, like a chore chart, a tip splitter or a packing checklist, and Claude builds a working version beside the chat. Ask for changes in plain words.
- [Let an AI sort and rename a messy folder of files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sort-and-rename-a-messy-folder/): Point a desktop agent at your Downloads folder or a drive full of oddly named files. It proposes a folder structure and clear names, then moves things only after you approve.
- [Turn rambling voice memos into tidy notes and a to-do list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-voice-memos-into-notes-and-tasks/): Talk into your phone while walking or driving, then let AI turn the transcript into organized notes, a to-do list and any drafts you mentioned.

### Small business & side hustles
All Small business & side hustles use cases: https://botsdothat.com/category/business/
- [Rebook all your clients after a surprise schedule change](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/rebook-your-clients-after-a-surprise-schedule-change/): When a surgery, a sick day or a family emergency wipes out your week, your bot moves everyone for you. It looks at when each client usually comes, offers each one a new slot that fits, updates the calendar when they say yes, and sends reminders the night before.
- [Hand your podcast or video edit to a team of AI agents](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-a-recording-into-an-episode-clips-and-posts/): Record your episode, then let a small team of agents do everything after: one plans the edit, one cuts short clips, one writes the captions and schedules the posts. Nothing goes live until you say yes.
- [Let your bot handle your website's contact email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-bot-handle-your-sites-contact-email/): Forward the contact address of your website, club or class to your bot's own email. It reads each message, sums it up for you, and only answers when you say so.
- [Put a small team of agents on one project, each with its own job](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/team-of-agents-with-roles/): Instead of one chatbot doing everything, give separate agents separate roles (one researches, one builds) and let them hand work to each other in a shared conversation you can watch.
- [Match every business expense to its receipt, weekly](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/small-business-receipt-matching/): A read-only bot checks your card and payment activity against the receipts in a dedicated inbox and lists what's missing.
- [Run several brands or jobs with one bot each](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/one-bot-per-brand/): If you juggle several brands or clients, give each its own bot with its own tools, plus a coordinator that collects a daily note.
- [Build a list of local leads and approve every email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-lead-list-with-approval/): A workflow finds businesses in your niche and area, researches each one and drafts a personal email. Nothing goes out until you approve it.
- [Log every new client inquiry automatically](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/log-new-client-inquiries/): When an inquiry email arrives, the bot pulls out the client's name and requested date, logs it in your tracker and sets up a folder.
- [Sell on Marketplace with an agent, with safety rules set first](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sell-on-marketplace-with-rules/): Agents can answer buyers and schedule pickups, but set rules first. One story tells of an agent sharing an address and booking a pickup when the seller was out.
- [Get your ads and sales numbers every morning without logging in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/daily-ads-and-sales-report/): A bot logs into your ad and sales dashboards (read-only) and sends a morning summary with what changed.
- [Write listings that sell your stuff faster](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sell-your-stuff-online/): You have things to sell, but writing listings, pricing them and answering buyers is a chore.
- [Test a side hustle idea before you commit](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/test-a-side-hustle-idea/): You have an idea to earn extra money, but you don't know if anyone will pay, and ads promise 'easy AI income'.
- [Reply to customer reviews (even the angry ones)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/reply-to-customer-reviews/): Reviews pile up on Google and you don't have time to answer, or a harsh review has you stuck on what to say.
- [Chase an unpaid invoice without burning the relationship](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/chase-an-unpaid-invoice/): A client is late paying and you're not sure how firm to be.
- [Turn a pile of PDF invoices and receipts into a spreadsheet](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-pdf-invoices-into-a-spreadsheet/): Drop in a stack of invoices or receipts and get one tidy table: date, vendor, amount and tax for each, ready for your bookkeeper or a spreadsheet.

## Latest in AI (newest first)
- 2026-11-26 [pricing] OpenAI fixes a GPT-6.2 billing mistake, so paid ChatGPT and Codex users hit limits up to 40% sooner; everyone gets one banked reset: If you pay for ChatGPT (Go, Plus, Pro or Business) and use GPT-6.2 Astra or Sol, the same work now uses more of your allowance: OpenAI says you'll reach your limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week, because a launch bug had been undercounting them; other models aren't affected and past usage won't be charged. As an apology every Go, Plus, Pro and Business account gets one banked reset, which you redeem in Usage settings on the web or desktop app (not mobile) once an allowance is below 80%, so save it for a day you're about to run out. Source: https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/chatgpt/weve-fixed-this-now-so-the-same-work-will-use-more-of-your-plans-usage-allowance-openai-admits-it-made-a-mistake-when-launching-gpt-6-2-and-now-paying-chatgpt-users-could-hit-their-usage-limits-up-to-40-percent-faster
- 2026-11-25 [feature] Gemini for Home update: faster smart-home commands, follow-ups like 'turn them back on', steerable bedtime stories and sources on displays: If you're in the Gemini for Home early access on a Google or Nest speaker or display, everyday commands like lights should respond faster, follow-ups such as 'turn them back on' now remember which lights you meant, and 'Hey Google, tell me a story' is back with stories you can change as they go. Google is also rolling out its improved Gemini Live ('Hey Google, let's chat') over the coming weeks, smart displays get a Sources button for web answers, and the Home app adds a remote 30-second siren on some outdoor cameras. Source: https://support.google.com/googlehome/answer/15962877?hl=en
- 2026-11-25 [pricing] From December, ChatGPT and Codex share one usage allowance on Plus, Pro and Business as Chat and Work merge: If you pay for ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Business, starting in December your chats, agent work and Codex coding will all draw from one allowance measured in tokens, so long agent or coding jobs can use up what you'd otherwise spend on chats; quick chats with the Instant model stay unlimited and don't count. OpenAI says most people won't wait for resets more often than now, but a spokesperson told TechCrunch a small share of the heaviest users may hit limits sooner; you'll see the combined total and reset times in Settings, then Usage, and a small group of Pro users already has the merged Chat and Work screen. Source: https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1042187/openai-is-combining-chatgpt-and-codex-usage-limits
- 2026-11-25 [feature] Guided Vision in Gemini Live comes to iPhone: point your camera and Gemini describes what it sees and tells you how to aim: If you're on an iPhone and are blind, have low vision or just can't read the small print, you can now share your camera in Gemini Live and get spoken descriptions plus cues like 'tilt down' or 'step back' until it can see what you asked about, such as a nutrition label, a washing-machine dial or a dropped earbud. It came to Android on Oct 1; Google says it can make mistakes and isn't a mobility aid or a replacement for a white cane. Source: https://x.com/GeminiApp/status/2125685936344236471
- 2026-11-25 [feature] OpenAI starts testing Private Inference, which keeps business prompts sealed off even while the model works on them: Nothing changes in your personal ChatGPT; this is for businesses: OpenAI is testing Private Inference (an alpha) with a small group of customers, running prompts and replies on sealed-off 'confidential computing' hardware with controls customers can verify, similar to how Apple handles Siri's cloud requests. Sam Altman announced the test on Nov 25; OpenAI gave no date for a wider rollout. Source: https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-private-inference-testing-customers
- 2026-11-25 [feature] Perplexity's Time Machine lets developers search the web as it was on a past date, up to a year back: Nothing changes in the Perplexity app; this is for people building or testing AI agents: Perplexity's Search and Context APIs can now show only the web as it was at a chosen date (up to 365 days back), so a research or forecasting agent can be graded on past questions without finding the answer that was published later. It costs the same as normal requests, $5 per 1,000 searches and $1 per 1,000 pages read. Source: https://www.unite.ai/perplexity-launches-time-machine-for-point-in-time-web-retrieval/
- 2026-11-24 [feature] Grok Bot 1.3 adds 'Notify me' restock alerts for sold-out products, Slack handoffs between Bots and an Ashby connector: If you shop with Grok Bot, a sold-out product card now has a Notify me button that watches that seller and tells you when the item is back, and if your X Money balance is too low the purchase is now refused before a card is issued, with the Bot asking you to add funds or pay another way. Version 1.3.0 also sends answers from one team Bot to another back to your Slack DMs, connects Microsoft Teams when you sign in with a work account and adds an Ashby connector for recruiting questions; Elon Musk is pitching Grok Bot this week for researching Black Friday deals and checking they're real. Source: https://x.ai/changelog/bot
- 2026-11-24 [industry] Google says AI agents must reach Gmail, Drive and other Workspace data through its MCP connectors from Feb 1, 2027: If an AI assistant or agent reads your Gmail, Drive, Calendar or Docs, Google now requires it to use Google's own MCP connectors or Workspace command-line tool instead of the regular APIs, enforced from February 1, 2027; agents that keep calling the old APIs directly will be held to the free tier's limits. Workplace admins also get agent audit logs, data-loss rules and the option to make you confirm sensitive actions like reading outside files or sharing data; the free Standard tier covers over 99% of developers, and a paid Scaled tier for heavy use starts billing on April 1, 2027. Source: https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/11/mcp-servers-cli-standardized-usage-tiers-now-available.html
- 2026-11-24 [model release] Cognition releases SWE-2.1 for Devin, free in Devin Desktop and CLI through Dec 8: Only matters if you use Devin for coding: Cognition's new SWE-2.1 model roughly doubles its predecessor's scores on coding tests such as Terminal-Bench 4.1 (50.0 vs 24.2) and is free in Devin Desktop and the CLI on Pro, Max and Teams through December 8, then $0.50/$2.50 per million input/output tokens through January 30, 2027 and $2/$10 after that. On Cognition's own charts it still trails Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol on most tests, and a version with looser safeguards, SWE-2.1 Cyber, is going to Devin Security. Source: https://cognition.com/blog/swe-2-1
- 2026-11-24 [agent launch] ByteDance's Doubao team opens an invite-only beta of Xiaodou, a separate personal AI agent app: Nothing to try outside China yet: Xiaodou is an invite-only public beta of a standalone personal assistant from the team behind ByteDance's Doubao chatbot, aimed at everyday tasks beyond work, and ByteDance calls it experimental with more abilities to come. It's one more sign that the big chat companies (Meta with Muse, Tencent, OpenAI with dots) are racing to give everyone an always-on personal agent. Source: https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-11-25/bytedance-expands-personal-ai-agent-push-with-xiaodou-beta-102508431.html
- 2026-11-24 [industry] New ShellBench test: even the best AI agents fail about 4 in 10 everyday jobs, and 1 in 6 runs breaks a safety rule: If you hand your bot real chores like matching receipts to a spreadsheet, planning a dinner or paying invoices, check its work before anything is sent or paid: on ShellBench's 100 everyday tasks built from real agent sessions, the top models (GPT-6 Astra 62.5%, Claude Fable 5.2 61.9%, GPT-6.1 Sol 61.4%) still missed a requirement about 4 times in 10, and the best one got the same task right on all three tries only 48.8% of the time. Across all 53,100 runs, 15.7% broke at least one safety rule, such as recommending a duplicate or wrong invoice payment or not withholding a sensitive bank token; the tests didn't use the Muse, Dots or Claude Duet apps themselves, so results there may differ. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/24/even-the-best-ai-agents-struggle-with-everyday-life/
- 2026-11-24 [industry] 42 state attorneys general ask a court to block Character.AI's auction of users' private chats: If you or your kids ever used Character.AI, your chat history, IP address and other account data are part of a bankruptcy auction set for December 1, and the buyer would not have to follow Character.AI's privacy policy or honour deletion requests, so consider deleting your account and chats now. California and a bipartisan group of 42 attorneys general asked the court on Nov 24 to reject the sale or at least leave out children's chats and other sensitive data; it's also a reminder that what you tell any chatbot can outlive the company. Source: https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-opposes-asset-sale-characterai-amid-child-safety-concerns
- 2026-11-24 [industry] OpenAI shows GPT-6 models can design new proteins that bind their targets in lab tests: Nothing changes in ChatGPT; it's a research result showing the same general models you chat with can do serious biology: GPT-6.2 designed small proteins using only reasoning and code, and in lab tests with Onava 35 of 322 designs (10.9%) stuck to their intended targets across five proteins, including one some cancers use to hide from the immune system. Specialised biology models still supplied the sequences and picked candidates, and it's a long way from a safe medicine, so don't read it as a new treatment. Source: https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/
- 2026-11-24 [industry] OpenAI posts a proof claim that multiplying matrices can never get faster than n^2.25, a famous open maths question: Nothing changes in ChatGPT and your apps won't get faster; it's another AI-lab maths claim to treat as unconfirmed for now: a 111-page OpenAI preprint says the 'speed limit' for multiplying large grids of numbers (the core sum behind AI itself) is exactly n^2.25, ruling out the long-hoped-for n^2. OpenAI's Lean computer check covers only part of the result (circuits without division), and outside mathematicians haven't reviewed it yet. Source: https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/The-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-nine-fourths-November-24-2026
- 2026-11-24 [industry] The UK competition watchdog asks people to report problems they've had with AI agents: If you live in the UK and an AI agent like Muse, ChatGPT dots or Claude Duet bought the wrong thing, misled you or was hard to cancel, you can now tell the CMA through an online form, anonymously if you like, with screenshots or other evidence. The CMA can't sort out individual complaints or give legal advice (go to a consumer advice service for that), but reports feed its oversight of the agents now launching in the UK. Source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tell-us-your-views-on-personal-ai-agents

## Blueprints
- [Morning Inbox Briefing](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/morning-inbox-briefing/): Wake up to a short summary of what's in your email and what needs you today.
- [School Email Digest](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/school-email-digest-bot/): Never miss a permission slip, payment or deadline buried in school emails again.
- [Web Page Watcher](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/web-page-watcher/): Get one ping when a page you care about changes (a restock, a new listing, an appointment slot, a status update) and stop refreshing it yourself.
- [Phone Call Bot](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/phone-call-bot/): Hand off the phone calls you keep putting off: booking a table, a vet visit or a haircut, or a quick customer-service call.
- [Scam Checker](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/scam-checker/): Get a plain verdict on suspicious emails and texts before anyone in the family clicks.
- [Weekly Meal Plan Bot](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/meal-plan-bot/): Get a family meal plan and one shopping list every week without thinking about it.
- [Family Calendar Guardian](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/family-calendar-guardian/): Spot clashes and prep jobs for the next two weeks, every Sunday.
- [Travel Day Guardian](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/travel-day-guardian/): Hear about schedule changes and delays first, with your options and a request ready to send.
- [Follow-Up Finder](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/follow-up-finder/): Never let a client, lead or friend go cold because you forgot to reply.
- [Job Match Scout](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/job-match-scout/): Get a daily shortlist of jobs that fit you, with notes. You apply yourself.
- [Receipt Matcher (small business)](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/receipt-matcher/): Have every business expense matched to a receipt before your bookkeeper asks.
- [New Inquiry Logger](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/lead-logger/): Every customer inquiry lands in one tracker with a reply drafted.
